old_problem: Fatal procedure wording conflicts with correctable criteria; railtype5/comparator semantics, management-versus-bulk input topology, full target expansion, executable syntax, reset policy and negative switchover oracle are absent.
disposition_reason: Severity and expected power-path behavior determine whether a reset or input transfer is a failure. They are not runtime identifiers. ED-03/12/15/18 require authoritative command, PASS and power-action semantics, so the case remains Pending/BLOCKED until the PMIC and platform owners reconcile them.
decision_basis: Read exact row94/history2492 and directly distinguished railtype5 input-only coverage from railtype4 bulk input and row95 railtype6 switchover.
Preserved the fatal label, correctable criterion, every DIMM, both voltage selectors, PMIC/I2C settings and OS evidence.
Required continuous active-input plus both-source telemetry so unintended transfer cannot be hidden by generic logs.
Required an explicit reset/no-reset decision and post-event rail/memory restoration.
No severity, source, address, syntax or timeout was guessed; no DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: DDR5 PMIC VIN management-input-only severity and path validation
test_case.purpose: Exercise each authorized VIN_Mgmt-only PMIC/comparator target, prove the intended severity while the management input remains selected or follows an explicitly approved alternative, and verify downstream power and memory remain healthy.
required_package: Approved fatal-versus-correctable severity and reset/no-reset behavior
Wistron BMC/platform I2C/OOB active-input observation path
Complete command/target matrix, electrical limits, event oracle and restoration procedure
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the split tuple. Once the severity and input-path contract is signed, baseline both input sources, active-input/status, downstream rails and memory; inject one mapped railtype5 comparator once; observe input selection and the approved reset policy; collect fresh source evidence, restore configuration and validate memory before another target.
test_case.expected_result: The selected PMIC records the authorized VIN_Mgmt-only event at the approved severity; reset and switchover behavior exactly match the decision, downstream rails stay within limits, the OS evidence is fresh, all DIMMs remain/recover healthy and state equals baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target/comparator identity, signed severity, continuous active-input evidence, approved reset/transfer outcome and complete recovery. Generic PMIC logs, unintended switchover, unexpected reset, unsafe rail, missing DIMM or state drift is FAIL/BLOCKED.
safety_gate: Instrumented isolated SUT with independent OOB and simultaneous VIN_Mgmt/VIN_Bulk/downstream telemetry.
One PMIC/comparator once; no target traversal.
Abort on ambiguous source selection, unsafe voltage/current/temperature, unexpected transfer/reset, I2C loss or memory failure.
No automatic retry, reset, failover or progression.
expected_evidence: Raw active-input, dual-source/downstream rail, status and memory baseline
Exact tuple/timeline with continuous input-select evidence
Fresh VIN_Mgmt-specific PMIC/CPER/SEL source and severity
Post-event rails, DIMM training/enumeration, bounded memory and restoration diff
test_case.recovery: Restore the approved PMIC input selection/mode/recovery, SPD control, telemetry, I2C and BIOS/HDT settings. Confirm both supplies and downstream rails, retrain/enumerate all DIMMs and run bounded memory health. Use the signed OOB path only if an unexpected transfer or reset occurred.

source_conflict.reason: Fatal versus correctable and reset/transfer behavior conflict; a fixed split tuple also cannot substantiate every DIMM/comparator.

blocked.reason: Without an input-selection and severity contract, injection may transfer or interrupt DDR5 power and an unexpected reset cannot be judged or safely recovered.
